narrative:
## Mode B — justified

The document makes checkable claims about existing code, and I verified each by reading rather than trusting it.

| doc claim | verified | where |
|---|---|---|
| `kit-index.sh` contains zero `python3` invocations | **TRUE** | `tooling/kit-index.sh` — external commands are git/awk/sqlite3/tr/sed/grep/sort/mktemp/find/date/cut/wc only |
| `tooling/kit_claims.py` does not exist | **TRUE** | `tooling/` holds `kit_findings.py` and nothing else `.py` |
| `kit_findings.py` is invoked on the write path | **TRUE** | `tooling/kit-finding.sh:43,83,173`, `tooling/kit-resolve.sh:414,421,426`, `tooling/kit-review-record.sh:48` — all emit-time |
| `kit-plan.sh:125` refuses a `--goal` outside `[letters digits . _ -]` | **SUBSTANTIALLY TRUE, cited wrong** | the guard is `case "$GOAL" in` at `tooling/kit-plan.sh:123` with the pattern at `:124`; `:125` is the first `kit_warn` line |
| the three quoted criticals are faithful | **TRUE** | `.project/index.db` `finding` rows `…:26925ff4`, `…:b032ddaf`, `…:65e3d2a2` match word for word |
| 627b9764 is latent — the two 2026-09-07 artefacts contain zero matching paths | **TRUE** | `docs/EXPERIMENTS/2026-09-07-claim-auditor-tier/arm-{opus,sonnet}.json`, zero `/home/…` or `/Users/…` matches under `validate.py:207-209`'s regex |
| "three of the **ten** open criticals" | **FALSE NOW** | six are open; five carry `fixed_at`, four of them stamped `2026-09-08T03:12` — after this document was committed (`9822e23` precedes `cd555bb`) |

One more state fact the document depends on and does not state: `.project/census/` **does not exist yet** and is **not gitignored** (`git check-ignore` clean), so the committed-artefact premise holds. `.project/index.db` is ignored and rebuilt, so the derived-table premise holds.

## Pass 1 — implementation-state audit and assumptions

| assumption | rating | what breaks |
|---|---|---|
| `unit` is a defined thing | **unstated-untested** | it is a component of **both** identifiers and is defined nowhere. `agents/claim-auditor.md:114-118` emits `source`, `subject`, `narrative`, `claims` — there is **no `unit` field**. Rev 2 names the file `<subject>.json`, so `unit` could be the filename, the `subject` string, or neither, and those are different values |
| `source_document` identifies the claim's document | **fragile** | rev 2 makes `source_document` a **manifest** (per-census) field while the artefact carries a per-unit `source` (`arm-opus.json` line 2: `"source": "docs/planning/ROADMAP.md"`). A census spanning two documents keys every claim to one of them |
| a hash is required for `claim_key` | **unstated** | never argued. The key is derived and table-local; a composite column set does the same work with no hash, no collision class, and no suffix/`id_ambiguous`/counter apparatus |
| the artefact is parseable by the derive path | **fragile, and load-bearing** | `kit-index.sh:816` `jf()` is `match(s, "\"" k "\"[ ]*:[ ]*\"[^\"]*\"")` — one string, one line, cannot see past an escaped quote (the `schema.sql` comment says so). The committed artefacts are pretty-printed, nested, with `\n` inside `narrative` |
| an ordinal read off an ordered array is stable | **defensible only if a real parser exists** | see above |
| dispositions do not need to cross censuses | **unstated-untested, and false against D3** | the whole point of D3 is re-running the same census. See Pass 2 |
| the artefact file is replaced atomically | **unstated** | the document names this itself as attack #1 and then does not answer it |
| `unit_sha` can be computed | **defensible, unspecified** | the kit's precedent is `git hash-object` (`kit-accel.sh:186`, `kit-spend.sh:127`). The document names no mechanism, no tool and no computing party |
| ADR 0004 governs drop-and-rebuild | **defensible** | ADR 0004's decision is "the plan is text, the index is derived from it, and only one thing writes each" — a fair paraphrase |

## Pass 2 — alternatives, compatibility, and the load-bearing behaviour

**The diagnosis is circular.** §"one name, two jobs" concludes *no single value satisfies both jobs*. That is only true under a premise the document never states: **re-keying must stay free**. A content hash computed once at capture and committed in a sidecar is content-derived (job 1) **and** frozen (job 2). It fails only the unstated third requirement. The document then presents free re-keying as the **payoff** of the split (§1, "Re-keying stays free because nothing committed names `claim_key`"). Premise and conclusion are the same sentence. This is precisely invited attack #2, and the "third form" the author says would falsify the document from the diagnosis down does exist.

**Alternatives not considered, one per major choice:**

- *identity*: **version the normalisation** — `hash(normalise_version, …)`, version recorded on the row. Old keys stay valid, new keys coexist, the diff matches on any version. This makes a committed content key re-keyable and collapses the split back to one identifier. Never mentioned.
- *identity*: **the disposition embeds its subject** — carry the claim text (or its hash at disposition time) in the event, so the record is self-describing and needs no live pointer at all. This dissolves `unit_sha`, the stale rule and the overwrite hazard together. Never mentioned. Note that ADR 0005's own rejection banner already recommends *"pinning evidence by git blob SHA (content-addressed, rename-immune, needs no normalisation)"* — the document cites neither ADR 0005 nor ADR 0006, both of which were written and rejected on exactly the question its new control re-decides.
- *matcher*: **no hash** — a composite text key over the derived table. Removes the collision apparatus the document deliberately keeps.
- *normalise*: **SQL** — the derive path already depends on `sqlite3` (17 invocations in `kit-index.sh`). `lower()`, `replace()`, `trim()` are deterministic and locale-independent there, one definition, no new dependency. The option table lists three mechanisms and omits the one already on the path.
- *normalise*: the table's own **option C is rejected on a reason that does not follow**. "Normalise at emit time in `kit-claim.sh`" does not entail writing the normalised value into the committed artefact; `kit-claim.sh` can write the artefact verbatim and a separate keys sidecar. The rejection argues against a different option.

**The option table is mis-costed at its foundation.** Every row prices *normalise*. But reading a claim, its ordinal, its verdict or its `source_loc` out of a verbatim pretty-printed nested artefact requires a JSON parser on the derive path **regardless of normalise**. `kit-index.sh` has none — `jf()`/`jn()` work on single-line, kit-emitted JSON with no escaped quotes. So option A's real cost is forced by the **artefact format** chosen in rev 2, not by the normaliser, and the closing fallback — *"if A is judged too expensive… accept a coarser matcher and say so in the diff output"* — is unavailable: without a parser there is no claim row to be coarse about. The recommendation section is arguing about the cheapest part of the bill.

**Contradiction with the design of record.** The document opens with *"It does not revise the census store design"*, then changes the key formula: rev 2 `:254` is `hash(subject_repo, source, subject, normalise(claim_text))`; this is `hash(subject_repo, source_document, unit, normalise(claim_text))`. Two of four components silently renamed. Meanwhile `2026-08-27-census-store.md` still defines `claim_key` with the ordinal (`:254`, `:266-270`), still states *"re-keying stays free forever"* (`:225`), and still says normalise is *"defined once, in `kit_claims.py`"* (`:272-274`) — with no cross-reference to this document. An implementer reading the store design gets the superseded design. The repo's own convention is in that same file: D1 carries a `> **Bounded by D4 below**` note at `:20-22` rather than being silently outranked. This document did not do the equivalent.

**AC ownership.** The split note at `.project/tasks/T-20260826-…:24-25` says *"AC4 and AC6 move to B and C respectively"*. The document's entire justification for job 1 is "**the store's** AC6" (`:26`). AC6 belongs to `T-20260828-census-diff-and-the-attribution-control-`. The identity decision binds a task this design input does not cover, and nothing lands on that task.

**Invariants preserved / broken.** `kit-event.sh:38` refuses six kinds *"the indexer acts on"*, and `tests/conformance.sh` derives that list from `kit-index.sh`'s dispatch so a seventh acted-on kind goes red rather than reopening the hole. `claim-disposition` is an acted-on, gate-affecting kind. The document never names this boundary, never says which writer validates `unit_sha`, and never says whether `kit_findings.py` or a new `kit_claims.py` serialises it.

## Pass 3 — blind-spot sweep

- **Observability** — **finding.** The stale-disposition control has no counter and no report surface. The document keeps `claim_id_collisions` as the precedent for saying ambiguity out loud, then builds a control whose firing is announced nowhere.
- **Failure modes (partial/slow/cascading)** — **finding.** A legitimate unit re-run (blessed at rev 2 `:247`, quoted approvingly here) permanently orphans every disposition on that unit. There is no re-anchor, no repair, no migration — only "stale, not applied". An `actioned` disposition carrying a task id becomes unreachable; a `false-positive` silently reverts to undispositioned.
- **Backpressure and resource limits** — **finding.** Every rebuild must hash every unit file of every census that carries a disposition, and censuses are never deleted (they are the benchmark corpus for D3). ADR 0006 measured this exact class: 21 `git cat-file -e` spawns = **9,432 ms, 24% of a 39s rebuild**; batched, 1,930 ms. `T-20260821-the-fixed-commit-walk-spawns-one-git-per` is already filed for it. The document costs none of this while agonising over an interpreter.
- **Operational lifecycle (startup/upgrade/rollback/drain)** — **finding.** Under option A, what does `kit-index.sh` do on a machine with no `python3` and a populated `.project/census/`? Skip (silently drops census rows and every disposition out of the gate — fail-open) or abort (breaks index rebuild for every adopter, including those who never ran a census)? Undecided.
- **Migration and mixed-version** — **finding.** There is nothing to migrate today (no census exists), but the 44 real rows in `docs/EXPERIMENTS/2026-09-07-claim-auditor-tier/` are named by the task as trial input and have **no `unit` field** to key on. The first thing this design would be tried against cannot supply a component of both its identifiers.
- **Security boundary and fail-mode** — **partly good, partly missing.** The stale rule denies rather than honours, which is the right direction. But `unit_sha` is supplied by the writer, so it defends against *silent drift*, not against an actor — and the document calls it "a control that can fail" without stating that threat model. The reserved-kind boundary (`kit-event.sh:38`) is unnamed.
- **Concurrency — is a check-then-act separated from its write?** — **YES, finding.** The operator reads the artefact to form the judgement; `kit-claim.sh --disposition` re-hashes the file when it writes the event. A `--unit` re-run landing between those two moments records a `unit_sha` that **matches** the new file for a judgement made about the old one. The control then passes and applies a disposition to the wrong claim — the exact failure it was built to prevent, inverted.
- **Testability** — **good, and the best part of the document.** "Seed a census, disposition a claim, overwrite the unit, rebuild, assert stale rather than applied" is a control that can fail. It is the only exit criterion offered, though: nothing tests the two-identifier split, the matcher, or option A.
- **Operational cost** — see backpressure. Also unaddressed: re-dispositioning cost. At 489 claims a census, if dispositions do not carry forward, every D3 re-run re-opens the entire judgement set.
- **Exit criteria** — **finding.** No criterion for "the identity question is settled". Given that `unit` is undefined, this document cannot currently be the evidence that closes `26925ff4`.

## The one that decides the verdict

**Disposition carry-forward is not addressed anywhere, and it falsifies the document's answer to `b032ddaf`.**

D3 says a census is a re-runnable reference; D2 says dispositions are the record a later contributor reads; rev 2 `:88-90` says dispositions must be retrievable *with their claim* as **content** of the discovery-session summary. Re-run census `aeon-2027-02-01` and every `claim_ref` from `aeon-2026-08-27` points into the old directory. Either (a) dispositions are census-local, in which case every re-run re-opens all 489 judgements and the record D2 exists to build resets on each use — a cost the document never names; or (b) they are carried forward by joining old-claim → `claim_key` → new-claim, in which case **what a committed disposition effectively names depends on `normalise`**, and changing it silently retargets carried-forward dispositions at different claims. That is `b032ddaf` verbatim, one join away.

So *"Re-keying stays free because nothing committed names `claim_key`"* is true about which bytes are on disk and false about which claims a committed record reaches. The document's headline answer to one of the three criticals it claims to close does not survive its own D3.

## Required changes before coding

1. **Define `unit`.** One sentence naming the exact field: the artefact's `subject`, the filename, or a new required contract field. If the contract must gain one, say so and file it against `T-20260826-no-agent-owns-verifying-documented-claim`. Resolve `source_document` (manifest, per-census) against `source` (artefact, per-unit) the same way.
2. **Decide disposition carry-forward across censuses, explicitly.** State whether dispositions are census-local or carried. If carried, withdraw the answer to `b032ddaf` and re-argue it — the join is the freeze. If census-local, cost the re-disposition burden against D2/D3 in the document.
3. **Re-cost the option table on the real bill.** Price JSON ingestion of a verbatim pretty-printed artefact, not normalise. Show why `jf()`/`jn()` cannot serve. Withdraw the "coarser matcher" fallback or explain how it obtains claims without a parser. Add SQL-in-`sqlite3` as option D, and re-argue option C against emit-time-normalise-to-a-sidecar rather than against writing into the artefact.
4. **Remove the positional component from the matching key, or stop claiming it is gone.** Analyse the deletion case: two byte-identical claims in one unit, one removed next census, survivor's suffix moves `:2`→`:1`, diff reports *disappeared + new*. `kit-index.sh:889-893` argues the suffix is safe **because the log is append-only**; census artefacts are not.
5. **Show that `claim_key` survives re-unitisation and document moves.** Two of its four components (`unit`, `source_document`) are organisational. Rev 2 itself leaves unit granularity open (`:402-403`). Either drop them, or state that a re-unitised census is not diffable and reconcile that with AC6.
6. **Pull `5c1284da` in.** `census_id` and `unit` are now identity components of a committed anchor, not just path components. The refusal rule is a precondition of this design, not a separable follow-on.
7. **Specify `unit_sha`:** who computes it, with what (`git hash-object` is the kit's precedent), batched or per-file, and the rebuild cost against ADR 0006's measurement. Close the check-then-act window between the operator's read and the writer's hash.
8. **Name the reserved-kind boundary.** `claim-disposition` must join `kit-event.sh:38`, with a named validating writer, or the operator-only rule is a convention.
9. **Decide index-time behaviour when `python3` is absent**, and say whether it denies or skips.
10. **Amend `2026-08-27-census-store.md` in place** with a bounding note at `:225`, `:254`, `:266-270` and `:272-274`, in the same style as its own D1/D4 note at `:20-22`. Cross-reference in both directions.
11. **Correct "ten open criticals" to six**, and record on `T-20260828-census-diff-and-the-attribution-control-` that AC6's matcher was decided here.

## Questions for researcher/operator

1. Is a disposition a judgement about **a claim** (must survive re-audit) or about **an observation of a claim** (census-local by design)? Everything above turns on this and the document does not ask it.
2. Why must `claim_key` be a hash at all, given it is table-local and disposable? Dropping the hash drops the suffix, `id_ambiguous` and `claim_id_collisions` with it.
3. Four criticals were marked fixed on 2026-09-08 at 03:12, including `794d0783` (*"normalise() is never specified"*). This document, written before those marks, says *"`normalise` has no mechanism, and the honest answer is that one must be built"*. Was `794d0783` closed on the text specification alone, with the mechanism deliberately left to `65e3d2a2`? Worth confirming rather than assuming — it is the shape the repo files against itself.
4. Are the 44 rows in `docs/EXPERIMENTS/2026-09-07-claim-auditor-tier/` intended to be keyable under this design? They have no `unit`.
5. Attack #1, unanswered by the document: is `kit-claim.sh --json` specified to write whole-file-atomically (temp + rename)? If not, `claim_ref` and `unit_sha` inherit the weakness together.

## What I did not check

- I did not run `kit-index.sh`, `tests/conformance.sh` or any rebuild; all state facts come from reading files and querying `.project/index.db`.
- I did not verify rev 2's other cited line numbers (`schema.sql:156-161`, `kit-index.sh:1001`, `kit-checkpoint.sh:17`, `tests/conformance.sh:2003-2097`, `claim-auditor.md:140`) — they belong to the earlier document, not this one. I did verify `kit-index.sh:872`, `:879-880`, `:881-904` and `2026-08-27-census-store.md:247` because this document leans on them.
- I did not assess whether `python3` is present on adopters' machines, nor read the workflow files to see how CI would behave under option A.
- I did not review task B's or task C's own design inputs, if any exist.
- I did not measure the derived-table build cost; rev 2 already records it as unmeasured.

findings.summary: `unit` is a component of both identifiers and is defined nowhere; the shipped contract emits `subject`, and the filename is a third candidate
claim_key uses source_document, a per-census manifest field, while each artefact carries its own per-unit `source`; a multi-document census mis-keys every claim
Disposition carry-forward across censuses is unaddressed; carrying them must join on claim_key, which is exactly the freeze b032ddaf named
The diagnosis is circular: no-single-value holds only under the unstated premise that re-keying must stay free, which is then sold as the split's payoff
The occurrence suffix is positional and stays in the matching key; deleting one of two identical claims renumbers the survivor into disappeared+new
Option table prices normalise only; ingesting verbatim nested artefact JSON needs a real parser, so python3 on the derive path is forced regardless
Option C is rejected for writing normalised text into the committed artefact, but emit-time normalise can write a sidecar; the rejection targets a different option
The stated fallback of accepting a coarser matcher is unavailable: with no JSON parser there are no claim rows, ordinals or verdicts to be coarse about
A legitimate unit re-run permanently orphans every disposition on that unit; no re-anchor or repair path is offered, only stale-and-not-applied
unit_sha is check-then-act: the operator judges the artefact, the writer re-hashes later, so an overwrite in between records a matching sha for a stale judgement
Per-rebuild hashing of every disposition's unit file is uncosted; ADR 0006 measured 21 git spawns at 24% of a rebuild, and censuses accumulate forever
claim-disposition is a kind the indexer acts on, so it must join kit-event.sh:38's reserved list; the doc names neither that boundary nor who validates unit_sha
5c1284da is deferred as separate while census_id and unit become identity components of a committed anchor; the refusal rule is a precondition, not a follow-on
Census-store rev 2 is left unamended and uncross-referenced: it still keys on the ordinal (:254,:266-270) and names kit_claims.py at index time (:272-274)
AC6 is called the store's, but the task's own split at :24-25 moved AC6 to task C; the identity decision binds a task this input does not cover
The alternative already on the derive path is missing: sqlite3 lower/replace/trim gives one deterministic normalise definition with no new dependency
Versioned normalisation is never considered as the third form that makes a committed content key re-keyable and collapses the split to one identifier
"ten open criticals" is stale: six are open, five carry fixed_at and four were marked on 2026-09-08 after this document was committed
"the same three mechanisms revision 2 proposed" is false of the key: source became source_document and subject became unit, silently
The stale-disposition control has no counter and no report surface, unlike the claim_id_collisions precedent the same document keeps
Under option A, index-time behaviour with python3 absent is undecided: skipping drops dispositions from the gate, aborting breaks rebuild for every adopter
Attack #1 is named and then left unanswered: nothing specifies that kit-claim.sh writes a unit file atomically as a whole
kit-plan.sh:125 is a warning message; the refusal guard is at :123-129, and the finding being answered cites :108-129
